name: Bellhop recurring jobs
description: Recurring definitions (code-, runtime- and configuration-defined), startup reconciliation, the atomic trigger on NextRunAt, misfire and overlap policies, time zones and DST, and runtime management. Each occurrence that starts creates a job in the jobs module.

entities.name: Occurrence
entities.description: One due instant of a recurring job and what was done about it.

ears.shall: evaluate a recurring job's schedule in UTC unless its time mode is Local, in which case it is evaluated in the IANA time zone the job names; Utc is the default time mode

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: all schedules are UTC (absolute) unless a job opts into Local time, for jobs that must run at a wall-clock hour in one place. Local mode needs an explicit IANA zone and never uses a node's own zone, because nodes in different regions would disagree (REQ-209, REQ-210). Daylight-saving rules apply only to Local jobs (REQ-228, REQ-229).

ears.shall: use RunOnce as the default misfire policy and Skip as the default overlap policy
record each recurring job's origin as code (attribute or AddRecurring), runtime (IRecurringJobManager or dashboard) or configuration (Bellhop:RecurringJobs)

ears.when: a node with the worker registered starts, or the scheduler finds a code-defined recurring job that a running worker node declares, and that job has no stored definition with its name
ears.shall: create the definition from the code definition of a node that declares it, with its schedule, time mode and zone, policies and payload, a hash of that code definition, and nextRunAt computed from now

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: recurring definitions belong to worker processes; a process without AddWorker neither reconciles nor declares them (hosting REQ-53 warns). refiner-model 2026-11-08 run 7 F-2 (option 2, chosen over making the orphan sweep compare heartbeats at its write): the scheduler reconciles in both directions, so stored definitions converge to what running nodes declare. A declared job that is not stored, because an orphan sweep raced a node starting during a rollback, a heartbeat was published late, or an operator removed an orphan just as it was declared again (REQ-213), is created again at the scheduler's next pass, active with nextRunAt from now. Instants while it was not stored are not missed (REQ-234), and an operator's pause of the removed job is lost with it.

sources.quote: On startup each node MUST upsert code-defined recurring jobs idempotently by name.

ears.when: a node with the worker registered starts and the hash of a code-defined recurring job's code definition differs from the definitionHash of the stored code-defined job with that name
ears.shall: update the stored definition and definitionHash to match the code, keeping its paused or active state, and, if the schedule changed, compute nextRunAt from now as in REQ-227

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: code is reapplied only when the code definition itself changed, so a runtime edit under AllowRuntimeOverride survives restarts and deploys that leave the code unchanged. During a rolling deploy, nodes on N and N+1 may rewrite a changed definition back and forth; the last writer wins, and once no running node's code matches the stored definition, REQ-241 brings it back to a running release (refiner-model run 2 F-2; before that, this note said it settles when the deploy ends, which fails after a rollback or a late restart of an old node). Keeping the paused state is confirmed. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-10 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): a schedule change that arrives with new code recomputes nextRunAt. F-6: applies only to a stored job of code origin; a runtime job with the same name stops the node instead (REQ-236).

ears.shall: never hold two recurring definitions with the same name, and never fail a node's startup because another node is reconciling the same definitions at the same moment

sources.quote: Multiple nodes starting simultaneously MUST NOT create duplicates or throw.

ears.when: the scheduler finds a stored code-defined recurring job that no running worker node declares
ears.if: the job's orphanPolicy is Orphan, the default
ears.shall: record the job's current state and mark it orphaned, which also pauses it, instead of deleting it

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: nodes publish the recurring names they declare with their heartbeat, as they do handler names (jobs REQ-124), so a job is orphaned only once no live node declares it. A rolling deploy therefore no longer flips it between Active and Orphaned. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-11 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): the orphan policy is a per-job attribute, orphanPolicy. Run 2 F-2: each published name carries the hash of its code definition, which REQ-241 uses.

sources.quote: A code-defined job removed from code MUST be marked Orphaned and paused, not deleted (configurable).

ears.when: the scheduler finds an orphaned recurring job that a running worker node declares
ears.shall: return the job to the state it had before it was orphaned, update the stored definition and definitionHash to match that node's code definition, and compute nextRunAt from now

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a job whose removal is rolled back comes back Active or Paused, as it was. Instants missed while orphaned are not caught up. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-5 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): a job that comes back with changed code takes the code definition at once. Run 5 F-1: instants already missed when the job was orphaned are recorded by the orphaning (REQ-242); only those that fall due while it is orphaned are dropped without a record. refiner-model 2026-11-08 run 8 F-1 (recommended option): the restore is the scheduler's, like REQ-203's scheduler branch, so it is obliged to happen. With actor Host nothing obliged it, so a job orphaned during a rollback, or by an orphan sweep that landed just after a node that declares it started (INV-212 notes), could stay orphaned until the next node start.

ears.when: the scheduler finds a stored code-defined recurring job that no running worker node declares
ears.shall: remove the definition

requirements.notes: Same event as REQ-205 with the complementary guard. The source only says the orphan behaviour is 'configurable'. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-11 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): the orphan policy is a per-job attribute, orphanPolicy. Run 7 F-2: the sweep judges 'no running worker node declares' from the heartbeats it read. If a node that declares the job starts before the removal lands (a rollback), the job is removed anyway, and REQ-203's scheduler branch creates it again once that node's heartbeat is published. That transient is accepted (INV-212 notes).

ears.when: an operator adds a recurring job through IRecurringJobManager or the dashboard and no definition with its name exists
ears.shall: create a runtime-defined recurring job with nextRunAt computed from now

ears.if: a schedule expression given through the API or the dashboard is invalid, or its time mode is Local without a valid IANA time zone
ears.shall: reject the call with an error that says what is wrong and store nothing

sources.quote: Invalid expressions MUST fail ... at the API call (runtime-defined), never silently.

ears.if: a code-defined or configuration-defined recurring job has an invalid schedule expression, or its time mode is Local without a valid IANA time zone
ears.shall: fail the host's start with a message that names the job and the problem

sources.quote: Invalid expressions MUST fail at startup (code-defined)

ears.if: an operator edits a code-defined recurring job through the API or the dashboard and the job is not marked AllowRuntimeOverride
ears.shall: reject the edit with a message saying the job is defined in code

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: 'edit' means changing the definition (schedule, time mode and zone, policies, payload). Pause, resume and trigger now are allowed on code-defined jobs; remove is refused (INV-206).

ears.when: an operator updates a runtime-defined recurring job, or a code-defined one marked AllowRuntimeOverride
ears.shall: store the new definition

ears.when: an operator removes a runtime-defined recurring job, or an orphaned one of any origin
ears.shall: delete the definition

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a code- or configuration-defined job that is not orphaned cannot be removed, because the next start would re-create it (INV-206).

ears.when: an operator pauses a recurring job through the API or the dashboard
ears.shall: mark the job paused

ears.when: an operator resumes a paused recurring job
ears.shall: mark the job active and compute nextRunAt from now

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: instants missed while paused are dropped, not caught up; 'from now' is confirmed. Maintenance is different: instants that fall due during maintenance go through the misfire policy (INV-210). refiner-model run 5 F-1: instants already missed when the job was paused are recorded by the pause (REQ-242); only those that fall due while it is paused are dropped without a record.

ears.while: a recurring job is paused or orphaned
ears.shall: never create an occurrence for it on schedule

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: 'trigger now' (REQ-226) is allowed while paused or orphaned; this rule covers only occurrences created on schedule.

ears.where: a recurring job has a validity window
ears.shall: never create an occurrence on schedule before ActiveFrom or after ActiveUntil

ears.while: a recurring job is active and maintenance is off
ears.when: its nextRunAt has passed according to the database clock
ears.shall: in one compare-and-set as INV-212 describes, advance nextRunAt to the next occurrence after now and create the occurrence or occurrences its misfire policy calls for

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-08 recurring run 6 F-1: the compare-and-set also covers the job's state, because a pause does not move nextRunAt. On nextRunAt only, a trigger that read the job as active could still land after a pause and create an occurrence for a paused job (INV-201). Run 7 F-1: it also requires maintenance to be off at the write. Maintenance is a separate flag, so a trigger that read the job just before an operator turned maintenance on still created its occurrence and advanced nextRunAt while maintenance was on (INV-210); now it loses, rereads, finds maintenance on and does nothing.

sources.quote: Triggering MUST be an atomic compare-and-set on the stored NextRunAt so that N nodes produce exactly one occurrence.

ears.shall: create at most one occurrence for each due instant of a recurring job, however many nodes run the scheduler

ears.when: a recurring job is triggered after one or more due instants were missed
ears.shall: create a single occurrence for all missed instants and, if the most recent due instant is on time, for that instant too

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: an instant counts as missed only when the trigger runs more than MisfireThreshold (60 s, REQ-234) after it; a slightly late trigger is on time (INV-207). refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-9 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): the newest due instant is judged on its own and the catch-up is merged into it, so one trigger never creates a catch-up plus an on-time run that the overlap policy would then skip.

ears.when: a recurring job is triggered after one or more due instants were missed
ears.shall: create no occurrence for the missed instants, create the occurrence of the most recent due instant only if it is on time (INV-207), and advance nextRunAt to the next future occurrence

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-9: the old 'only advance nextRunAt' contradicted INV-207 when the newest instant was on time.

ears.when: a recurring job is triggered after one or more due instants were missed
ears.if: the misfire policy is RunAll with a maximum
ears.shall: create one occurrence per missed instant and one for the most recent due instant if it is on time, keeping the most recent of them up to that maximum, and log the older instants it dropped

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the newest instants are kept. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-9: the on-time instant counts toward the maximum.

ears.when: a recurring job is triggered after one or more due instants were missed
ears.shall: log how the missed instants were handled and why, and raise the recurring-missed event

requirements.notes: The event is consumed by IJobEvents (jobs REQ-169). Notifications (integrations REQ-403) read the stored record of REQ-242 instead, so a miss is still alerted after a lease handover or while no alerts node runs (integrations INV-412).

ears.when: an occurrence is created and no earlier occurrence of the same recurring job is waiting or has an unfinished job
ears.shall: enqueue a job with the recurring job's payload and record the occurrence as started

requirements.notes: Recurring jobs may carry a payload, so one job type can have many recurring instances, for example one per tenant (REC-8). Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: 'still running' means the occurrence's job is unfinished, as defined in REQ-239. A run waiting to retry therefore blocks the next one. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): a waiting occurrence is also in the way, so a new occurrence never starts ahead of one that is still waiting. F-7: Unroutable no longer counts as unfinished (REQ-239).

ears.when: an occurrence is created while an earlier occurrence of the same recurring job is waiting or has an unfinished job
ears.shall: start nothing and record the occurrence as skipped

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1: a waiting earlier occurrence counts as in the way, the same as an unfinished job.

sources.quote: Skip (default: do not start if the previous run is still active; record a Skipped occurrence)

ears.when: an occurrence is created while an earlier occurrence of the same recurring job is waiting or has an unfinished job
ears.if: the overlap policy is Queue and fewer occurrences than its maximum are waiting
ears.shall: record the occurrence as waiting for the earlier ones to finish

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: Queue takes a maximum of waiting occurrences, 1 by default (REQ-233); beyond it occurrences are skipped (REQ-235). refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1: a waiting earlier occurrence counts as in the way, the same as an unfinished job.

ears.when: no earlier occurrence of the same recurring job is waiting or has an unfinished job
ears.shall: enqueue a job for the waiting occurrence and record it as started

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-2 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): waiting occurrences start one at a time in creation order, each only once every earlier occurrence is finished and none is still waiting, so Queue(max) is a FIFO with one runner whatever the maximum. Replaces 'when the earlier occurrence's job succeeds, is dead-lettered or is cancelled', which released every waiting occurrence at once.

ears.when: an occurrence is created while an earlier occurrence of the same recurring job is waiting or has an unfinished job
ears.if: the overlap policy is Allow or CancelPrevious
ears.shall: enqueue a job for the new occurrence and record it as started, and under CancelPrevious also request cancellation of the earlier occurrence's job

requirements.notes: Under CancelPrevious the two runs overlap until the earlier handler honours its token. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1: a waiting earlier occurrence counts as in the way, the same as an unfinished job.

ears.where: a recurring job's overlap policy is Skip or Queue
ears.shall: never have two of its occurrences' jobs in the Processing state at the same time

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-3 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): restated in terms of job states in the store. An abandoned or lease-lost handler can still run beside the next occurrence (REQ-238).

sources.quote: enforced by the store across nodes

ears.shall: never fail a job, throw an exception or wait on a lock timeout because of an overlap decision

sources.quote: No distributed lock timeouts, no exceptions.

ears.when: an operator triggers a recurring job now, optionally with an overridden payload
ears.shall: create an occurrence immediately, using the overridden payload if one was given, decide it by the overlap policy like a scheduled occurrence, and leave nextRunAt unchanged

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the overlap policy applies, nextRunAt does not move, and it is allowed while the job is paused or orphaned because it is an explicit operator action.

ears.when: a recurring job's schedule changes
ears.shall: compute nextRunAt from now, never from the last execution, and create no catch-up occurrence for the old schedule

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-07 run 4 F-1: no catch-up still holds, but instants that were already missed when the schedule changes are recorded as dropped (REQ-242), so the miss is alerted. Run 5 F-2: that includes an instant that passed moments before the change and was not triggered yet (REQ-234).

ears.where: a recurring job's time mode is Local
ears.when: its next occurrence falls on a local time skipped by a daylight-saving change
ears.shall: run it once at the next valid instant

ears.where: a recurring job's time mode is Local
ears.when: its next occurrence falls on a local time repeated by a daylight-saving change
ears.shall: run it once, at the first instance of that time

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the first instance. Interval schedules are INV-208.

ears.when: an operator asks for a recurring job's next N occurrences
ears.shall: compute them from its schedule in its own time zone

ears.when: an occurrence's job succeeds, is dead-lettered or is cancelled, or an occurrence is skipped
ears.shall: record that outcome as the recurring job's last outcome

ears.where: recurring jobs are defined in configuration under Bellhop:RecurringJobs
ears.when: that configuration changes
ears.shall: apply the added and changed definitions without a restart

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: configuration-defined jobs are treated exactly like code-defined ones (INV-209): removed from configuration means orphaned once no live node declares it, read-only in the UI unless AllowRuntimeOverride, and hot reload reconciles like a start. Nodes with different configuration settle as in a rolling deploy.

sources.quote: Recurring jobs MAY also be defined in configuration (Bellhop:RecurringJobs) with IOptionsMonitor hot reload

ears.shall: allow at most MaxQueuedOccurrences waiting occurrences per recurring job under the Queue overlap policy, 1 by default (MaxQueuedOccurrences)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: configurable per job as Queue(max).

ears.shall: treat a due instant as missed when the trigger runs more than MisfireThreshold after it, 60 seconds by default (MisfireThreshold), or, for an instant that fell due while the recurring job was active, when no trigger ran for it before nextRunAt was moved past it or the job stopped being active, however recently it fell due

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06; same default as Quartz. refiner-model run 5 F-2 (recommended option): 'missed' was defined only by when the trigger runs, so an instant that had just passed when a schedule change, pause, orphaning or removal passed over it was neither run nor missed, and left no trace. Now every instant that passed while the job was active either runs on time or is missed and recorded (REQ-242). Instants that fall due while a job is paused or orphaned are not missed; they are dropped on purpose (REQ-215, REQ-206).

ears.when: an occurrence is created while an earlier occurrence of the same recurring job is waiting or has an unfinished job
ears.if: the overlap policy is Queue and its maximum of waiting occurrences is already reached
ears.shall: start nothing and record the occurrence as skipped with reason QueueFull

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Same event as REQ-222, REQ-223 and REQ-225 with a complementary guard. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1: a waiting earlier occurrence counts as in the way, the same as an unfinished job.

ears.if: a code-defined or configuration-defined recurring job has the name of a stored runtime-defined recurring job, judged by each stored recurring job's name and origin only, with none stored where the store has no Bellhop schema yet
ears.shall: fail the host's start with a message that names the job and says it is already defined at runtime

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-6, decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: recurring job names are unique across origins, and a collision is an error on both sides (INV-211 for the API). Like REQ-210. hosting run 3 F-1 (recommended option): the check runs before the migration (hosting REQ-12), so it must work on whatever schema is stored. Name and origin are stored by every schema version, because migrations only add (TECH-127); a new database has no Bellhop tables and so no runtime-defined jobs, which must not fail the first start.

ears.when: a recurring job is paused, orphaned or removed while it has waiting occurrences
ears.shall: record each waiting occurrence as skipped with reason Paused, Orphaned or Removed

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-8 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): pausing, orphaning and removing drop the waiting occurrences, so nothing starts for a job that is no longer active.

ears.shall: not prevent a handler that was abandoned on timeout or lost its lease from still running while the next occurrence's job runs (the at-least-once window, jobs REQ-10)

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-3 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): INV-204 is a rule about job states in the store; this item records the overlap it cannot prevent (jobs REQ-132, REQ-138, REQ-186).

ears.shall: treat an occurrence's job as unfinished for overlap decisions while it is not Succeeded, DeadLettered, Cancelled or Unroutable

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-7 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): an Unroutable occurrence job no longer blocks its recurring job for good; the next occurrence is decided by its own handler availability and becomes Unroutable too, which the dashboard shows. Before this, the definition (without Unroutable) lived only in REQ-221's notes and the glossary, which are not semantic. Run 2 F-1: because jobs REQ-125 brings an Unroutable job back when a handler appears, the newer occurrence cancels it when it starts (REQ-240), so the two never run side by side.

ears.when: an occurrence of a recurring job starts while an earlier occurrence of the same recurring job has an unroutable job
ears.shall: cancel that unroutable job with reason Superseded in the same write that starts the new occurrence

requirements.rationale: REQ-239 lets the next occurrence start past an Unroutable job, but jobs REQ-125 returns that job to Enqueued as soon as a handler appears, which is exactly when the newer job becomes runnable too (INV-204).
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 run 2 F-1 (recommended option; checked by the model over 262,576 states with all four overlap policies). The newer occurrence replaces the stale one, which is what Skip and Queue intend, so under Skip and Queue a recurring job never holds more than one Unroutable job and only one runs when a handler comes back. Under Allow and CancelPrevious, jobs started side by side can all become Unroutable and all run when it comes back, which those policies permit (run 4 F-3). Cost: the stale occurrence's run is lost; the cancel reason says why. jobs REQ-134 already allows cancelling an Unroutable job, so the jobs module needs no change. Run 3 F-1 (recommended option): the sentence applies to every start under every overlap policy, including Allow and CancelPrevious starts under REQ-225, so whether a stale job is superseded never depends on whether some other earlier job happens to be unfinished. Run 3 F-2 (recommended option, accepted): an earlier trigger-now occurrence (REQ-226) is superseded like a scheduled one, even with an overridden payload; the operator sees reason Superseded and triggers it again once the handler is back. Exempting it would either block the schedule behind its Unroutable job again (run 1 F-7) or let it run beside the newer job (run 2 F-1).

ears.when: the scheduler finds a stored code-defined recurring job that running worker nodes declare but whose definitionHash matches the code definition of none of them
ears.shall: update the stored definition and definitionHash to the code definition of one of those nodes, keeping its paused or active state, and, if the schedule changed, compute nextRunAt from now as in REQ-227

requirements.rationale: REQ-204 runs only when a node starts, so after a rollback, or after an old node restarted late in a deploy, the stored definition can belong to a release that no running node runs.
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 run 2 F-2 (recommended option). Nodes publish each declared name with the hash of its code definition in their heartbeat, as they already publish the names (REQ-205); the check runs with the orphan sweep, a worker duty (hosting REQ-40). While the stored hash matches any running node's code nothing changes, so there is no back-and-forth during a deploy while at least one node of the new release stays up (if all of them are down at once while old nodes run, the old definition is written back and the new one again when a new node returns, refiner-model run 3), and the definition settles as soon as the old release is gone. A runtime edit under AllowRuntimeOverride does not change definitionHash, so it survives.

ears.when: an active recurring job's nextRunAt is moved past one or more missed due instants, by a trigger (REQ-216) or by a schedule change (REQ-227), or an active recurring job is paused (REQ-214), orphaned (REQ-205) or removed (REQ-207, REQ-213) while it has missed due instants
ears.shall: record in the job store which due instants were missed (the first, the last and how many) and how they were handled (the occurrences the misfire policy created for them and whether each started, is waiting or was skipped by the overlap policy, or that the misfire policy, the schedule change, the pause, the orphaning or the removal dropped them), in the same store write that moves nextRunAt or pauses, orphans or removes the job, which is a compare-and-set that judges the missed instants by the database clock at that write (INV-212), and keep that record as long as dead-lettered jobs are kept (jobs RetentionDeadLettered)

requirements.rationale: integrations INV-412 makes the notification lease holder find missed occurrences in the job store. The last outcome (REQ-231) is overwritten by the next one, and RunOnce leaves no trace of a miss at all.
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 integrations run 3 F-17 (recommended option). One record per trigger, not per instant, so a long outage on a frequent schedule writes one record. REQ-220's log line and in-memory event are unchanged. Run 4 F-1 (recommended option): a schedule change applied at a node start (REQ-204), by the scheduler (REQ-241) or by an operator (REQ-212) moves nextRunAt past overdue instants without a trigger (REQ-227); those instants are recorded as dropped by the schedule change, so integrations REQ-403 alerts them. Before, whether a missed run left any trace depended on whether the deploy also changed the schedule. Instants that fall due while a job is paused or orphaned are dropped on purpose and not recorded (REQ-215, REQ-206). Run 4 F-2 (recommended option): the record says what became of each catch-up occurrence, because the overlap policy can skip it in the same write, and a record saying only "caught up by RunOnce" then reported a run that never happened. Run 5 F-1 (recommended option): instants already missed when an active job is paused, orphaned or removed are recorded in that write. A pause, orphaning or removal does not move nextRunAt, and the later resume or restore happens while the job is not active, so before this those misses left no trace, depending on whether the trigger or the operator came first. Run 5 F-2: 'missed' covers an instant that passed moments before any of these writes and was not triggered yet (REQ-234), so every instant that passed while the job was active either runs or is recorded. Run 5 F-3 (recommended option): the record describes each occurrence as it was in the write that made it; a waiting occurrence may later start (REQ-224) or be skipped (REQ-237), which the record does not follow. The occurrence's own state says what became of it. Run 6 F-1 (recommended option, widened to every write): run 5 made the pause, orphan and removal writes decide the record from what they read, but nothing made them conditional on it, so a trigger that landed in between ran the instant on time and the pause still recorded it as dropped, and integrations REQ-403 alerted a miss that did not happen. Every write that changes the job's state or nextRunAt is now one compare-and-set on both (INV-212).

ears.if: an operator removes a code-defined or configuration-defined recurring job that is not orphaned
ears.shall: refuse with a message that the job would be re-created at the next start

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.when: a recurring job is triggered no more than MisfireThreshold after its due instant
ears.shall: treat the instant as on time and create its occurrence whatever the misfire policy

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06, so Skip never drops a run that is only a poll interval late.

ears.where: a recurring job has an interval schedule
ears.shall: fire it at fixed elapsed-time intervals, whatever its time mode and across daylight-saving changes

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: Local mode only affects cron-style 'at a wall-clock time' schedules.

ears.where: recurring jobs are defined in configuration under Bellhop:RecurringJobs
ears.shall: reconcile, orphan and protect them from runtime edits and removal exactly as code-defined jobs (REQ-203 to REQ-207, REQ-211, INV-206)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.while: the global maintenance pause is on
ears.shall: never create an occurrence on schedule and never advance nextRunAt by a scheduled trigger, so that instants missed meanwhile go through the misfire policy when maintenance ends

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06 (scope of maintenance, jobs INV-114). Unlike a paused job (REQ-215), missed instants are not dropped. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-4 (decided 2026-11-06, recommended option): narrowed to the scheduler. Operator and reconciliation actions during maintenance (REQ-206, REQ-215, REQ-227) keep their own 'from now' rules.

ears.if: an operator adds a recurring job through IRecurringJobManager or the dashboard with a name that is already stored
ears.shall: reject the call with an error that names the existing job and its origin, and store nothing

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-6, decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: names are unique across origins and a collision is an error on both sides (REQ-236 for starting nodes).

ears.shall: make every store write that changes a recurring job's state, nextRunAt or definition, or removes the job (a trigger, a schedule change, a definition update by REQ-204, REQ-212 or REQ-241, a pause, a resume, an orphaning, a restore or a removal), a compare-and-set on the state, nextRunAt and definition it read, and for a trigger also on maintenance being off, which judges due and missed instants by the database clock at that write and changes nothing if any of them changed since the read, after which the writer reads the job again and decides anew

requirements.rationale: Every one of these writes decides what it does from what it read: whether an instant runs, whether it was missed, what REQ-242 records, and whether the schedule changed. A write that lands after another one changed any of that acts on a job that no longer exists in that form. The rule is that a write is conditional on everything it decided from, except the heartbeats (notes).
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-08 run 6 F-1 (recommended option, applied to every write instead of the pause alone). The model split the pause into its read and its write: unconditional, a trigger that landed in between ran the 02:00 instant on time and the pause still recorded it as dropped, and integrations REQ-403 alerted a miss that did not happen; a schedule change in between got the instant recorded twice. Recurring writes all follow this one rule rather than each getting a phrase of its own, because the same race also exists in the other direction. A trigger that read the job as active could land after a pause, which does not move nextRunAt, and create an occurrence for a paused job (INV-201); an orphan sweep or a schedule change that read an active job could land after a pause and record its missed instants a second time. The other direction, the orphan, removal, schedule-change and resume writes, and the reread after a lost compare-and-set have not been model-checked yet (SCN-216, SCN-217). A trigger that loses does nothing on its reread, because another node advanced nextRunAt (SCN-200). REQ-226's trigger-now changes neither value, so it is not covered. How a store judges at the write is TECH-45. Run 7 F-1 and F-3 (recommended options, combined): a trigger also decided from maintenance (INV-210), and a definition update decided from the stored schedule whether nextRunAt moves, so both are now in the condition; without them a trigger read just before maintenance turned on still fired, and a REQ-241 update that read an unchanged schedule landed after an operator's schedule edit and left nextRunAt from the edit beside the code schedule, skipping some 20 hours with no record. In a store, the state, nextRunAt and definition are one row version. Run 7 F-2 (option 2): the heartbeats are not part of the condition. The orphan sweep, a restore and a REQ-241 update decide from the declarations they read, and one that changed before the write is corrected at the scheduler's next pass: a job removed while a node that just started declares it is created again (REQ-203), a job orphaned that way is restored (REQ-206), and a definition taken from a node that has just stopped is updated again (REQ-241). The same holds for REQ-203's scheduler create, which can land after the node it took the definition from has stopped; the next pass orphans, removes or updates it as the declarations then say. Comparing heartbeats at the write was not chosen: it needs a cross-table condition, and a node's declarations are published some time after it starts anyway, so it would also need a hosting ordering rule to be complete.

glossary.misfirePolicy: RunOnce (default: one catch-up), Skip (jump to the next future occurrence) or RunAll(max) (REQ-217 to REQ-219).
glossary.overlapPolicy: Skip (default), Queue(max), Allow or CancelPrevious (REQ-221 to REQ-225, REQ-235).
glossary.timeMode: Utc (default) or Local; Local needs an explicit IANA time zone (REQ-200).
glossary.MisfireThreshold: Lateness of the trigger after which a due instant counts as missed; 60 s by default. An instant that an active job's schedule change, pause, orphaning or removal passes over before any trigger ran for it is missed however recently it fell due (REQ-234).
glossary.MaxQueuedOccurrences: Waiting occurrences allowed under Queue; 1 by default (REQ-233).
glossary.unfinished: For overlap: the occurrence's job is not Succeeded, DeadLettered, Cancelled or Unroutable (REQ-239). A waiting occurrence is also in the way (REQ-221 to REQ-225, REQ-235).
glossary.orphanPolicy: What happens to a code- or configuration-defined job no live node declares: Orphan (default, REQ-205) or Delete (REQ-207).
glossary.Orphaned: A code- or configuration-defined job that no live node declares; kept and paused, and restored to its earlier state if declared again (REQ-205, REQ-206).
